$comment: Budgets enforced by scripts/perf-audit.mjs (Lighthouse 13 no longer ships --budget-path). Scores are 0-1, metrics are milliseconds except cumulative-layout-shift, resource sizes are transferred kilobytes of the site's own resources (a third party's bytes count only as third-party requests). Initial values are regression budgets for the starter baseline; raise them only with a note in docs/performance.md. A route under `routes` takes its own values for the keys it names.

resources.$comment: Third-party requests: every page loads Google Tag Manager's container script from Google (the owner's decision, 2026-11-21; docs/architecture.md, 'Analytics'), one request, and the budget leaves room for a Google Analytics tag and its beacons once the container has one. Anything beyond that in the container is a new decision.

/.$comment: Mobile LCP only, for a measurement effect and not the page: the home page's LCP element is the hero image, and Lighthouse's simulation counts Google Tag Manager's container script as an LCP dependency whenever the script starts executing before the hero is shown, which GitHub's runner does in some runs (2657 and 2754 ms counted, 1653 ms not; the Mac 1652 ms, never counted). Not permission for the page to get slower: a local audit of / above 2500 ms is still a regression to fix. Remove it with Tag Manager, or if the script moves. docs/performance.md, decision log, 2026-11-21.

/contact/.$comment: The contact page embeds Calendly's scheduler (the owner's decision, 2026-11-20; docs/architecture.md), an iframe that fetches Calendly's own scripts and styles and Stripe's, and whose cookies fail Lighthouse's third-party-cookies audit (best practices 0.77 measured). The allowances are for that embed and the Tag Manager script every page loads (17 third-party requests measured, 2026-11-21): the page's own resources keep the budgets above.

/privacy/.$comment: SEO score only: the privacy policy is a draft (the owner's request, 2026-11-22), and while `draft` in src/data/privacy.ts is true the page is noindex on purpose, which Lighthouse's is-crawlable audit, the only one that fails, counts against SEO (0.66 measured). Remove this with the noindex once the policy is approved. docs/performance.md, decision log, 2026-11-22.
